measures.short_title: Apply public records law to Legislature and governor
measures.summary: Makes most records of the governor's office and the state Legislature subject to the public records law, ending their current exclusion.
measures.threshold_note: Initiative statute: majority of votes on the question AND yes votes at least 30 percent of all ballots cast.
measures.campaign: Backed by Auditor Diana DiZoglio's Committee for Transparency and Democracy and the Coalition for Healthy Democracy, which raised about $5.2M across Q1 and Q3; no organized opposition filed.

polls.note: UMass Amherst ballot numbering differs from official; matched by content. Yes/No combine definitely+probably. 3 pct said they did not understand.

measures.short_title: Collective bargaining for public defender agency staff
measures.summary: Lets Committee for Public Counsel Services employees, including public defenders, unionize and bargain collectively, and raises bar advocate pay.
measures.threshold_note: Initiative statute: majority of votes on the question AND yes votes at least 30 percent of all ballots cast.
measures.campaign: Labor Unions for Public Counsel Workers Rights supports; no organized opposition filed; supporters spent at least $1M.

polls.note: UMass Amherst ballot numbering differs from official; matched by content. Yes/No combine definitely+probably. 13 pct said they did not understand.

measures.short_title: Single all-party primary, top two advance
measures.summary: Replaces party primaries for state offices with one primary listing all candidates, with the top two finishers advancing to the general election.
measures.threshold_note: Initiative statute: majority of votes on the question AND yes votes at least 30 percent of all ballots cast.
measures.campaign: Coalition for Healthy Democracy (Danielle Allen) spent nearly $5M, top donors Randy Peeler over $1M and Andrew Balson nearly $800K; opposed by state Democratic and Republican parties and Voter Rights MA.

measures.short_title: Change state revenue cap and rebate excess
measures.summary: Bases the state tax revenue limit on prior year actual net state revenue plus wage and salary growth and rebates revenue above the limit to taxpayers.
measures.threshold_note: Initiative statute: majority of votes on the question AND yes votes at least 30 percent of all ballots cast.
measures.campaign: Massachusetts Opportunity Alliance business coalition (Taxpayers for an Affordable Massachusetts) about $1.9M in-kind; labor unions (Protect Massachusetts' Future) over $700K opposing.

polls.note: UMass Amherst ballot numbering differs from official; matched by content. Yes/No combine definitely+probably. 10 pct said they did not understand.

measures.short_title: Create Nature for All conservation fund
measures.summary: Creates a Nature for All Fund for conservation and recreation, dedicating sales tax revenue from certain sporting goods, recreational vehicles and golf courses, roughly $65M a year.
measures.threshold_note: Initiative statute: majority of votes on the question AND yes votes at least 30 percent of all ballots cast.
measures.campaign: Led by Mass Audubon; no organized opposition filed; supporters spent at least $1M.

polls.note: UMass Amherst ballot numbering differs from official; matched by content. Yes/No combine definitely+probably.

measures.short_title: Allow single-family homes on smaller lots
measures.summary: Requires municipalities to allow single-family homes on residential lots of at least 5,000 square feet with 50 feet of frontage served by public water and sewer; Boston excluded.
measures.threshold_note: Initiative statute: majority of votes on the question AND yes votes at least 30 percent of all ballots cast.
measures.campaign: Legalize Starter Homes supports, spent at least $1M; Massachusetts Municipal Association opposes.

polls.note: Pre-certification Feb wave, support/oppose wording on a 5 point scale. PDF tables were misaligned in text extraction; yes is from the release narrative. Only the 36 pct support figure is reported reliably; high undecided.

measures.short_title: Repeal recreational marijuana sales
measures.summary: Prohibits retail sales of recreational marijuana, repeals home cultivation, and sets new possession limits and civil penalties; medical marijuana unaffected.
measures.threshold_note: Initiative statute: majority of votes on the question AND yes votes at least 30 percent of all ballots cast.
measures.campaign: Coalition For a Healthy Massachusetts funded mostly by SAM Action Inc. (nearly $3.2M); Massachusetts Cannabis Coalition and industry opposing with almost $1.6M.

measures.short_title: Keep or repeal 2024 gun law
measures.summary: A Yes vote keeps the 2024 firearms law (H.4885), which expanded the assault-style firearm ban and other rules; a No vote repeals it.
measures.threshold_note: Referendum on existing law: the law is repealed only if No wins a majority AND No votes are at least 30 percent of all ballots cast; Yes keeps the law.
measures.campaign: Vote Yes for a Safe Massachusetts supports keeping the law; The Civil Rights Coalition (gun rights groups) leads repeal.

polls.note: UMass Amherst ballot numbering differs from official; matched by content. Yes/No combine definitely+probably.

measures.short_title: Require budget to fund state worker contracts
measures.summary: Requires the governor's budget to fully fund state employee collective bargaining agreements, including terms set by a neutral arbitrator (HB 604, Arbitration Reform for State Employees Act of 2026).
measures.threshold_note: Simple majority.
measures.campaign: Backed by state employee unions; no organized campaign or money reported in sources reviewed.

measures.short_title: Temporary appointments to judicial disabilities commission
measures.summary: Allows temporary substitute or recalled members on the Commission on Judicial Disabilities when a member is recused or a term expires.
measures.threshold_note: Simple majority.
measures.campaign: No organized campaign reported.

measures.short_title: Remove constitutional limits on congressional districting
measures.summary: Limits districting requirements to state legislative districts, sets no constitutional criteria for congressional maps, and lets the General Assembly give the Supreme Court of Maryland original jurisdiction over congressional map challenges; enables mid-decade congressional redistricting.
measures.threshold_note: Simple majority. Ballot text rewritten by Supreme Court of Maryland order of Sept 3, 2026.
measures.campaign: Fight Back Maryland, Gov. Wes Moore, Democrats and unions support; Protect Maryland Votes (spokesman Doug Mayer) opposes; passed in August 2026 special session; no money totals found.

measures.short_title: Eliminate elected register of probate office
measures.summary: Removes the register of probate from the constitution's list of elected county officers (CACR 13).
measures.threshold_note: Two thirds of those voting on the question. A similar 2022 amendment got 62.9 percent and failed.
measures.campaign: Passed House 325-15 and Senate 23-1; no organized campaign.

measures.short_title: Constitutional right to collective bargaining
measures.summary: Adds a constitutional right for employees to organize and bargain collectively, barring laws that interfere with it, effectively banning right-to-work laws.
measures.threshold_note: Simple majority.
measures.campaign: Yes on 3 (Rep. Conor Casey) and Vermont AFL-CIO support; Right for Vermont Foundation opposes; no money totals reported.
